passages.title: 4. Obstructions and controls
passages.text: 4. Obstructions and controls The input-product premise cannot be dropped. Let \(a=b=x\), \(h=1\), and \(c=1-r_0x-r_1(1-x)\). From the two companions one derives \(c=E_0+E_1\). Nevertheless the Boolean/domain system with these companions has the solution \(x=1,r_0=1,r_1=0\), where \(c=0\) and \(b=1\). Thus the implication derivation alone does not give an old derivation of \(b\). Under zero replay, its first companion requires the missing product \(bx=x^2\). In (MP-BC), the antecedent derivation supplies that product; it cannot be silently omitted. A later dependent block is not an old axiom. If a retained block has input \(c\), its companion \(c(1-sc)\) changes to \(1-s\) when \(R_U=0\). Our replay cannot use that new polynomial as the unchanged old axiom. This explicit dependency is a failed hypothesis of the present method, not a proof that no method can handle multiple levels. Some degree loss for old consequences is necessary in general. For the single field variable \(x\), let \(\mathcal G=\{x^2,x^p-x\}\). Its minimum PC degree for deriving \(x\) is exactly \(p\): multiply \(x^2\) to obtain \(x^p\), then subtract \(x^p-x\). Below degree \(p\), that field axiom cannot be introduced, and every obtainable polynomial remains in the ideal \((x^2)\), which does not contain \(x\). Add an accuracy-one block with input \(x\) and companion \(E=x(1-rx)\). Then \(x=E+rx^2\) has an augmented derivation of degree three. For \(p\ge5\), degree-preserving old-consequence elimination is therefore false. This is a field-domain control, not a Boolean PHP instance or an asymptotic obstruction for a fixed prime. Prefix and spread controls. Setting \(t=1\) in (BC) recovers the known one-block charge on the prefix-pebbling refutation . The stronger existing nested-span replay still removes its whole chain for one charge, and its base still has PC degree at most three . The new argument neither upgrades ordinary designs to PC-annihilating functionals nor turns high NS degree into high PC degree. Appending unused spread blocks changes none of the used line degrees or selected input degrees; they can be pruned under the existing certificate rule. Neither control gives an affordable bound for all essential surviving blocks. These comparisons use the recorded proofs; no historical suite was rerun.

passages.title: 3. A control where products are easier than the factor
passages.text: 3. A control where products are easier than the factor For any two affine inputs \(f,g\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), take \[ \beta_f=1+g,\qquad\beta_g=1,\qquad H=(1+f)(1+g). \] Then \[ fH=(f+f^2)(1+g),\qquad gH=(g+g^2)(1+f). \] An affine polynomial \(f=a_0+\sum_v a_vy_v\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) satisfies \(f^2-f=\sum_v a_v(y_v^2-y_v)\). The displayed companion products therefore have original-domain certificates of degree at most three. This is an explicit rank-two instance of the earlier substitution method and a positive control for the new solver. We use the first two inputs of saved spread space zero. Their factor \(H\) is not in the base degree-two consequence space: otherwise these coefficients, extended by zeros to the full input tuple, would contradict its preceding normalization obstruction . Thus this control actually distinguishes cheap companion products from a cheap factor.

passages.title: 1. Ordinary clauses and the truth-value convention
passages.text: 1. Ordinary clauses and the truth-value convention Let \(P_{ij}\) mean that pigeon \(i\) uses hole \(j\), with \(n+1\) pigeons and \(n\ge2\) holes. Ordinary PHP is the negation of the conjunction of the clauses \[ R_i^{\mathrm{cl}}=\bigvee_{j=1}^nP_{ij},\qquad C_{aa',j}^{\mathrm{cl}}=\neg P_{aj}\vee\neg P_{a'j} \quad(a<a'). \] There are no same-row exclusion clauses. We use total symbol length \(S\) for the proof-size parameter; it bounds both the number of lines and the formulas whose approximations are introduced. The source translates an atom \(P_{ij}\) to a Boolean algebraic variable \(q_{ij}\), with TRUE represented by zero. Our incidence variable \(x_{ij}=1\) means that \(P_{ij}\) is true, so make the global affine change \[ q_{ij}=1-x_{ij}. \] Consequently the atom approximation is \(1-x_{ij}\), its negation approximation is \(x_{ij}\), and \(q_{ij}^2-q_{ij}\) becomes exactly \(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij}\). The source's exact, unapproximated disjunction translation is multiplication. Thus the exact translation of a row disjunction has degree \(n\). Applying Theorem 6.7(1) directly to those assumptions would leave its input parameter \(d_0\) as large as \(n\), which does not provide the required polylogarithmic degree. The following replacement addresses that parameter explicitly.

6. Checks and the remaining obstruction

The compiled exact checker verified 12 nonlinear field-selector cases over \(p=2,3,5,7\), with ranks one, two, and three and mixed field/Boolean old-variable domains. It saved all 48 image certificates from the original univariate domain equations. Omitting one required scalar selector failed all 78 controls.

Eight Boolean-packing cases used inputs that were themselves products of earlier ENS blocks. They retained 20 explicit earlier-companion certificates. Six odd-prime controls gave a nonzero image on the bare domain grid when the parent companion equations were omitted, confirming that those earlier equations are essential to this stronger packing argument. These examples are symbolic extension data, not PHP refutations.

The syntax checker built the complete MOD recursion AST with three argument disjunctions of widths 17, 19, and 23. It found exactly the six schema blocks in the table, with maximum arity three, and detected the increase to 24 after double-negation simplification. The argument blocks remain explicitly present in the saved graph.

Four expanded specialized MOD-axiom polynomials, one for each tested prime, have fully reconstructed NS certificates from \(t^p-t,a^2-a\). All 34 points of the corresponding field/Boolean grids satisfy them. The interpolation errors and their domain certificates are also saved. Complete polynomials, domain cofactors, earlier-companion cofactors, AST nodes, and controls are in checks-01.jsonl; the result record specifies reproduction and coordinates.

Why wide implication blocks still need work. A natural attempt to replace a flattened \(A\vee B\) block by the product \(ab\), where \(a=P_{G_A}\), \(b=P_{G_B}\), uses the identity \(1-ab=(1-a)+a(1-b)\). Its coefficients can be written using the two earlier telescoping vectors. But for disjoint affine child tuples at accuracy \(h\), the original flattened product has degree \(2h\), whereas \(ab\) has degree \(4h\). A companion image can therefore have degree \(4h+1\) against original degree \(2h+1\). Moreover, the argument blocks can be at the same ENS level as the flattened parent. This does not satisfy the earlier-level, original-degree image hypotheses just used.

Source-construction cleanup before that step. The established ordinary-PHP bridge uses MOD-row derivations that introduce wide row-prefix disjunctions. They are artifacts of that prelude. The simulation proof's induction also derives the approximation of a theorem directly; combining that with the existing clause certificates may avoid the prelude. Establish this direct construction first, then investigate relative transfer for the remaining wide blocks \((a,G_B)\) and \((a,b,G_C)\), with their same-level dependencies and image-degree costs kept explicit.

Suppose the available elimination transformations have degree charges \(c_A,c_B\). passages.title: 3. Why a selector for one input need not handle another block
passages.text: 3. Why a selector for one input need not handle another block A small exact control isolates the missing simultaneous-image premise. Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) with only the Boolean domains of independent variables \(x,y_1,\ldots,y_t\) as old axioms. Take one block on \((x)\) and another on \((y_1,\ldots,y_t)\), the latter with accuracy \(h<t\). In the nonzero branch of \(x\), the weight is \(\chi_1(x)=x\). For arbitrary scalar choices \(\beta_{u,i}\) in the second block, put \[ Q_\beta(y)=\prod_{u=1}^{h} \left(1-\sum_{i=1}^{t}\beta_{u,i}y_i\right). \] If every weighted second-block companion \(xy_iQ_\beta(y)\) were an old-domain consequence, then setting \(x=1\) would force \(Q_\beta(y)=0\) at every nonzero Boolean \(y\). At \(y=0\), its value is one. Its unique multilinear Boolean representative would therefore be \[ \prod_{i=1}^{t}(1-y_i), \] of degree \(t\). Boolean reduction cannot increase degree, whereas \(\deg Q_\beta\le h<t\), a contradiction. At the boundary \(h=t\), one coordinate per coefficient row gives exactly this product, so all the weighted companions do vanish. This is the same Boolean-grid degree argument already used in the constant-normalizer controls , applied to the proposed replay. Scope. This satisfiable domain example is not an augmented refutation and is not the full PHP base. It refutes the claim that a branch selector automatically supplies domain proofs for unrelated blocks, even when there are only two blocks. It does not refute one-block elimination, polynomial coefficient choices, use of additional base equations, a different joint functional, or a theorem exploiting an actual PHP refutation. Replacing the failed scalar step by one of those mechanisms requires its own argument and cost.

passages.text: 4. A small row/column cover supplies actual-degree images For a tuple of signed literals in residual cells, form its support graph, ignoring repeated occurrences. If its edges are covered by \(k\le h\) row or column vertices, assign each nonzero literal occurrence to one covering vertex. Each group is supported in a single row or column, where the functional base supplies Booleanity and pairwise exclusions. The earlier one-column literal formulas apply verbatim to either kind of star. For completeness, write the variables of one star as \(Y_i\). If a constant one or both signs of one variable occur, scalar coefficients make its factor zero. Otherwise, with two distinct negative literals \(1-Y_v,1-Y_w\), coefficients \(1,Y_v\) give the factor \(Y_vY_w\), a star-exclusion axiom. With exactly one negative \(1-Y_v\), use coefficient one on it, giving factor \(Y_v\); all positive companions are exclusions and its negative companion is Boolean. With only positives, use one coefficient per distinct variable, giving \[ q_s=1-\sum_{i\in A}Y_i,\qquad Y_vq_s=-(Y_v^2-Y_v) -\sum_{i\in A\setminus\{v\}}Y_vY_i. \] Unused repeated coordinates receive zero. Thus every coefficient image is a field constant or a single residual variable, and every group input \(g_i\) has an NS image certificate for \(g_iq_s\) through degree at most three. The coefficient-field images have certificates through degree \(p\). Empty or all-zero groups need no factor. Assign one original coefficient row to each group, with all other coefficients zero. Then the block product is \(\prod_{s=1}^{k}q_s\), where each factor has degree at most two. For an input in group \(s\), multiply its local certificate by the other factors. Its full companion image has NS cost at most \[ 3+2(k-1)=2k+1\le2h+1, \] which fits the original degree of every nonzero literal companion at accuracy \(h\). A block already containing a constant-one input is removed by assigning coefficient one to it in one row, making the whole product zero. All-zero tuples give zero companions with zero coefficients.

passages.title: 1. The first product sampler and its cost
passages.text: 1. The first product sampler and its cost One preliminary option is a sum of independent products of \(t\) random affine forms over \(\mathbb F_p\). For any nonzero linear functional \(\psi\) on \(\mathcal P_{\le t}\), its value on one such product is a nonzero multilinear tensor in the \(t\) independent coefficient blocks. Nonzeroness follows by selecting a product of variables and constants on which \(\psi\) is nonzero. Condition on the first \(t-1\) blocks. Averaging a nontrivial additive character over the last block gives zero if the resulting linear form is nonzero, and one otherwise. By induction, a nonzero tensor in \(t-1\) blocks is nonzero with probability at least \(\theta_p^{t-1}\), where \(\theta_p=1-1/p\): choose a nonzero coefficient tensor and, when it survives, a nonzero linear form takes a nonzero value with probability \(\theta_p\). Thus the character average lies in \([0,1-\theta_p^{t-1}]\). Summing \(L\) independent products multiplies these averages, giving error at most \(\exp(-L\theta_p^{t-1})\). It suffices to take \(L\ge\theta_p^{1-t}\log(1/\varepsilon)\), at circuit cost \(O(vtL)\). This is exponential in \(t\). The following construction removes that loss.

passages.title: Exact verified statement
passages.text: Exact verified statement Let \(R\) be any nontrivial commutative ring, and let \(t,a\) be independent indeterminates in \(R[t,a]\). For every natural number \(p\ge3\), there exists \(Q\in R[t,a]\) such that \[ (t+a-1)^{p-1}-a t^{p-1}-(1-a)(t-1)^{p-1} =(a^2-a)Q,\qquad \deg_{t,a}Q\le p-3. \] For \(p=2\), the left side is identically zero over every commutative ring, without a nontriviality assumption. Primality and characteristic \(p\) are unnecessary. In particular, taking \(R=\mathbb F_p\) gives the complete earlier interpolation claim. The degree is total degree in both variables; neither Boolean reduction in \(a\) nor field reduction in \(t\) is used.

passages.title: Verified statement and indexing
passages.text: Verified statement and indexing For any commutative ring \(A\), finite index set \(I\), inputs \(f_i\in A\), and coefficients \(r_{v,i}\in A\), use zero-based rows and define \[ P_h=\prod_{v=0}^{h-1}\left(1-\sum_{i\in I}r_{v,i}f_i\right),\qquad U_{h,i}=\sum_{v=0}^{h-1}r_{v,i}P_v. \] Then \(1-P_h=\sum_i U_{h,i}f_i\) for every natural \(h\), including zero. Reindexing rows by \(v\mapsto v+1\) gives exactly the source's displayed coefficients. The proof allows empty input sets and repeated inputs without identifying their indices. For the degree statements let \(A=R[\mathbf x]\), an ordinary multivariate polynomial ring over any commutative ring \(R\). Suppose \(\deg f_i\le\delta\) and \(\deg r_{v,i}\le1\) for \(v<h\). The formalized bounds are \[ \deg P_h\le h(\delta+1),\qquad \deg U_{h,i}\le1+(h-1)(\delta+1),\qquad \deg(f_iP_h)\le\deg f_i+h(\delta+1). \] For \(h\ge1\), these use ordinary integer arithmetic as displayed. Lean also permits \(h=0\), with natural subtraction truncated at zero and \(U_{0,i}=0\). Mathlib assigns total degree zero to the zero polynomial, which causes no issue for these nonnegative upper bounds. The source's nonzero-input degree assumption therefore implies the formal hypothesis for all inputs. Fresh coefficient indeterminates have degree one and are a special case. No Boolean or field reduction, freshness, or nonvanishing assumption is needed for these upper bounds.

passages.title: The indexed rule-convention bridge
passages.text: The indexed rule-convention bridge If either premise entails \(D\), use that semantic weakening. This includes a tautological \(D\), and handles degenerate zero-dimensional cases without invoking a separator. Otherwise apply the dependency above. At a point satisfying \(A\) but falsifying \(D\), soundness implies membership in \(Z(B)\), so \(u=1\). Similarly, a point satisfying \(B\) but falsifying \(D\) has \(u=0\). Therefore \[ A\models D\vee(u=1),\qquad B\models D\vee(1-u=1). \] Two weakenings produce these clauses and one complementary-parity resolution produces \(D\). The Lean inductive derivation system has only premise nodes, semantic weakening, and this resolution rule. It counts new inference nodes and proves both soundness and existence of a derivation with at most three new nodes. It does not include arbitrary binary semantic inference as a rule, so the result is not circular. The two intermediate clauses form a finite set of cardinality at most two; each adds at most one literal to \(D\). Finite sets identify repeated literals and coincident intermediate clauses automatically. Every added literal is still an affine function on the original space. Precomposing all clause forms with any affine map preserves satisfaction and therefore preserves the binary semantic consequence. This includes fixing fresh propositional variables to constants.

passages.text: 3. The natural collision-relative control is an existing mechanism The column-state normalizer already gives degree-preserving coefficient maps for arbitrary polynomial inputs in a single unary PHP column, using its collision equations. That was the first natural positive candidate in this cycle, so it is treated as reused work. Its compact binary version is transparent. For a fixed label \(\lambda\), let \(\chi_i\) be the degree-\(\ell\) Boolean indicator that pigeon \(i\) has label \(\lambda\). Then \[ \chi_i\chi_j-\chi_i E_{ij}\in\mathcal I_{2\ell}({\rm BOOL}), \qquad \chi_i\chi_j\in\mathcal I_{2\ell}(\mathcal Q_n). \] The first polynomial vanishes on the Boolean cube and has degree at most \(2\ell\), so ordinary Boolean division supplies its certificate. For \(v_\lambda=1-\sum_i\chi_i\), \[ 1-v_\lambda=\sum_i\chi_i,\qquad \chi_i v_\lambda =-(\chi_i^2-\chi_i)-\sum_{j\ne i}\chi_i\chi_j \in\mathcal I_{2\ell}(\mathcal Q_n). \] Binary Booleanity of \(v_\lambda\) fits \(2\ell\). Thus the literal old-input tuple has a cost-\(\ell\) PHP-relative profile. If it comes from label-selector bottoms of original weight \(2h\), \(2h\ge\ell\), retain input bounds \(2h\) and profile cost \(2h\), rather than silently resetting those source bounds. This is not a Boolean-domain-valid profile: at an assignment where exactly two pigeons have label \(\lambda\), \(v_\lambda=1\) and the corresponding companion is nonzero. The collision equation supplies the missing certificate. This shows that the escape from cycle 149 is real, but it does not enlarge the general source coverage beyond the existing column mechanism.

passages.title: 4. Checks that did not supply the general step
passages.text: 4. Checks that did not supply the general step A sparse-support refinement would not address the complete source boundary. If all collision residuals in a profile package involve only \(q\le n\) pigeon rows, fix those rows to distinct labels. Those residuals vanish, the remaining affine helpers stay affine, and the package becomes Boolean-domain-valid on \(v'=v-q\ell\) free bits. The restricted approximate-majority circuit still has the two Hamming balls of radius at least \(\lfloor v/3\rfloor-q\ell\). For \(q=o(n)\), the previous obstruction remains linear in \(v'\). However the actual compact-clause boundary uses all pigeon pairs, so its residual support is already global. Developing this sparse condition would not discharge the current obligation. A targeted primary-source check also prevented a misleading literature inference. Lu, Santhanam, and Tzameret (2025) study a DNF family expressing hardness of algebraic proof lower bounds. Their abstract states that small \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege proofs fail infinitely often, while whether that DNF family consists of tautologies remains open. This is not an unconditional lower bound for a known PHP tautology family. Only the versioned abstract and scope were checked; no theorem from its diagonalization proof is imported.

passages.title: H: the precise prior-literature claim
passages.text: H: the precise prior-literature claim The new indexed target third-party:BLVZ-chessboard-filling is the needed consequence of Björner–Lovász–Vrećica–Živaljević, Theorem 1.1 . Let \(\mathcal M_k(s,N)\) be the set of \(k\)-cell matchings on an \(s\times N\) board: finite cell sets with injective row and column projections. Put \(C_k=\mathbb F_2^{\mathcal M_k(s,N)}\). These are chains of reduced simplicial degree \(k-1\); in particular \(C_0\) is the empty-face augmentation coordinate. For \(k\ge1\), define the boundary by \[ (\partial_k c)(T)=\sum_{\substack{S\in\mathcal M_k(s,N)\\T\subset S}}c(S) \qquad(T\in\mathcal M_{k-1}(s,N)). \] All incidence signs are one over \(\mathbb F_2\). The boundary from \(C_1\) sums the vertex coefficients; the outgoing map at \(C_0\) is zero. The target is \[ s\ge2,\ N\ge2s-1,\ c\in C_{s-1},\ \partial_{s-1}c=0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \exists b\in C_s:\ \partial_s b=c. \] MathResearch.ThirdParty.ChessboardFilling in ChessboardFilling.lean defines exactly this proposition. Faces use Fin s × Fin N , chains are functions on the finite face type, and the boundary tests codimension-one inclusion. The zero-cell-count branch of the boundary definition handles the augmentation endpoint; H itself restricts to \(s\ge2\). A transparent face-type abbreviation permits Lean to infer finiteness. There is no declaration asserting H, no custom axiom, and no sorry . The general boundary-squared-zero proof remains a planned task.

Face correspondence and cardinality preservation give maps on every graded supported-chain space. Pull after push is the identity by injectivity. passages.title: Full certificate argument
passages.text: Full certificate argument For every \(n\ge1\), \(X_i^n-X_i\in\mathcal I_n(\mathrm{BOOL})\). At \(n=1\) the polynomial is zero. Induct using \[ X_i^{n+1}-X_i=X_i^{n-1}(X_i^2-X_i)+(X_i^n-X_i). \] The new generator multiple has ordinary degree at most \(n+1\), and the earlier witness remains legal at this larger ceiling. To reduce a product of positive powers, induct over its variables with \[ AB-ab=A(B-b)+(A-a)b, \qquad A=X_i^{e_i},\quad a=X_i,\quad B=\prod_{j\in S}X_j^{e_j},\quad b=M_S. \] The first error has certificate cost at most \(e_i+\sum_{j\in S}e_j\). The second has cost at most \(e_i+|S|\), which is no larger because all exponents indexed by \(S\) are positive. Here multiplying an existing ordinary NS witness uses the already verified R02 multiplication closure, which multiplies each legal generator multiple and charges its actual degree. Therefore \(X^e-M_{\operatorname{supp}(e)}\) has certificate cost at most \(\sum_i e_i\). Scalar combination over the monomials of \(P\) gives the stated witness through \(\deg P\). No Boolean quotient degree replaces an original polynomial degree. Each \(M_S\) has individual degrees at most one and total degree at most \(|S|\). Since \(|\operatorname{supp}(e)|\le\sum_i e_i\), the remainder has the asserted total-degree bound. At a point of \(\mathbb F_2^V\), every positive power of a coordinate equals that coordinate, proving pointwise agreement.

passages.text: Grid injectivity and boundary cases The formal proof reuses Mathlib's checked finite-field evaluation injectivity. A complete argument for that step is as follows. For \(v=|V|\), the squarefree polynomial space has the \(2^v\) squarefree monomials as a basis. The space of functions on \(\mathbb F_2^V\) also has dimension \(2^v\). Evaluation is onto, since the point \(a\) has the squarefree indicator \[ \delta_a(X)=\prod_{i:a_i=0}(1-X_i)\prod_{i:a_i=1}X_i. \] Thus evaluation between these equal-dimensional spaces is an isomorphism. A zero-evaluating squarefree polynomial is zero. Applied to the remainder, this proves the vanishing certificate. passages.text: All row equations, with the original degree charge For a matching \(T\), if row \(i\) is unused, the extension \(T\cup\{(i,j)\}\) is a matching exactly when column \(j\) is unused. Thus \[ \mathcal R(M_T(\rho_i-1))= \sum_{j\notin\operatorname{col}(T)}M_{T\cup\{(i,j)\}}-M_T. \] If row \(i\) is occupied at \((i,j_0)\), the only surviving term of \(\rho_iM_T\) is \(j=j_0\), which reduces to \(M_T\), so the displayed product reduces to zero. Both assertions are checked as polynomial identities. An annihilator of the full system annihilates \(\mathcal A\), hence has the same value on \(P\) and \(\mathcal R(P)\) whenever \(\deg P\le B\). If \(|T|<B\), then \(M_T(\rho_i-1)\) is a legal multiple through \(B\). Applying the preceding identity therefore proves every stated marginal equation. For the converse, take a linear functional annihilating \(\mathcal I_B(\mathcal A)\) whose matching moments satisfy the marginals. It annihilates every matching-monomial row multiple of cardinality below \(B\): use the unused-row identity and its marginal, or the occupied-row zero identity. Now consider any legal ordinary row multiple \(q(\rho_i-1)\) through \(B\). If \(q=0\), there is nothing to prove. Otherwise \(\rho_i-1\) is nonzero and has actual degree one because \(N\ge1\): one of its variable coefficients is one. The polynomial ring is an integral domain, so \[ \deg(q(\rho_i-1))=\deg q+1\le B. \] Multiplying the normal-form witness for \(q\) by \(\rho_i-1\) therefore stays in \(\mathcal I_B(\mathcal A)\). The functional has the same value on \(q(\rho_i-1)\) and \(\mathcal R(q)(\rho_i-1)\). The latter is a linear combination of the matching-monomial row multiples already checked, since every surviving support has size at most \(\deg q<B\). This exhausts all legal generators and then their span. The argument subtracts an actual degree, not a loose ceiling. For \(N=0\), the row generator would instead be the degree-zero constant \(-1\), so this reverse argument correctly does not assert that extra case.

passages.title: Ordinary NS transport with every generator multiple charged
passages.text: Ordinary NS transport with every generator multiple charged Let \(\mathcal F\) and \(\mathcal G\) be source and residual polynomial systems. Assume that for every \(f\in\mathcal F\) there is one fixed \(g_f\), either zero or an actual generator of \(\mathcal G\), such that \(\sigma_\varepsilon(f)=g_f\) for every cube choice. Then \[ \Delta(qf)=\left(\sum_\varepsilon\sigma_\varepsilon(q)\right)g_f =\Delta(q)g_f. \] For one legal ordinary NS generator multiple \(qf\) of actual degree at most \(B\), its image is zero if \(g_f=0\). Otherwise it is the displayed multiple of the supplied residual generator, and its actual ordinary degree is at most \(\max(0,B-r)\), by applying the proved degree-drop theorem to \(qf\) itself. Thus it is a legal residual NS multiple through that ceiling. Linearity and induction over the original NS span prove \[ \Delta\bigl(\mathcal I_B(\mathcal F)\bigr) \subseteq\mathcal I_{\max(0,B-r)}(\mathcal G). \] This accounts for every original generator multiple before summation; it does not allow cancellation between illegal higher-degree source multiples or subtract an inflated generator-degree budget. Consequently any residual functional annihilating the latter NS space gives a source annihilator by composition with \(\Delta\). Verification and scope. BinaryCubeDegreeDrop.lean defines the actual cube homomorphisms and their linear sum, proves cancellation and ordinary-degree loss, proves fixed-factor extraction, and transports NS certificates and annihilators. The final fourteen-declaration audit checks the version bounding only untagged images; the preliminary all-image-bound audit is retained separately. Scope and source provenance record the evidence. This is a project-formulated finite-difference interface for the cube proof, without a novelty claim. Remaining work and process assessment. R14 still requires its concrete board substitutions, proof that every unary generator has the stipulated cube-independent residual image, and isolation of the chosen coefficient in the actual R13 row-linear space through the R12 decoder. These hypotheses have not been assumed to declare R14 complete. The explicit operator separates the ordinary-degree argument from the board combinatorics, and removing the bound on ignored tagged-variable images gives its natural general scope. No framework rule or optional post-route sweep was added; no mathematical discrepancy was found.

passages.text: 4. The previously missing query detects the difference On the distinguished row, the bit-only density from the earlier counterexample was \(\theta p_C\), where \(p_C\) has value one at labels \(0,1\) and \(\bar\theta\) elsewhere. It agreed with the true parent component on bit queries through five. The old unary variable \(X_{0,0}\), however, is an additional degree-one query, and \[ \lambda_*\bigl((\theta p_C-X_{0,0})X_{0,0}\bigr)=1. \tag{ROW-new-query} \] The unscaled old projection \(p_C\) also fails orthogonality to the full input ideal: pairing \(p_C L_1X_{0,1}\) gives \(\bar\theta\ne0\). Replacing it by \(X_{0,0}\) repairs these tests and the mixed port. No row-state mass was changed. The earlier counterexample is still valid in its original bit-only space; the corrected old space contains more low-degree information.

passages.title: What is generic, and what still depends on the source
passages.text: What is generic, and what still depends on the source The finite DAG registry theorem is generic but requires actual bounded-degree derivations of the supplied initial clause values. For a CNF with \(t\) initial clauses of width at most \(w\), take the old base to contain its ordinary clause polynomials \(F_C=\prod_i(1-g_i)\) and Boolean equations, with \(g_i\) the literal true-indicators. The telescoping identity gives \[ P_C=F_CP_C+\sum_i\left(\prod_{j<i}(1-g_j)\right)g_iP_C. \] Each term has a PC/NS certificate through \(w+2h\): the clause product has degree at most \(w\), the block product at most \(2h\), and each prefix-companion product at most \(w+2h\). The empty initial clause directly supplies one. Hence an \(S\)-node source refutation gives a registry with at most \(3S+t\) slots and a refutation through \(D=\max\{4h+1,w+2h\}\). Applying the preceding theorem gives a generic subspace-consequence bound. For another old encoding, an analogous initial-value bridge must be supplied; \(D=O(\log n)\) is not free for arbitrary wide clauses or arbitrary encodings. The publication uses its specific compact bit-PHP bridge. The conclusion is not in general a degree-\(B\) PC refutation: the resulting polynomial is some nonzero \(f\), not necessarily one. Nonzero ordinary polynomials can be valid low-degree consequences. For instance, the satisfiable system \(\{x,x^2-x\}\) derives the nonzero polynomial \(x\) but cannot derive one. Thus this argument alone does not establish a conventional universal size-versus-PC-refutation-degree theorem or a Res(\(\oplus\)) size–width relation. A useful application needs a sufficiently large space \(U\) with the additional separation property \(U\cap\mathcal C_B=\{0\}\). In bit PHP that is the substantial row-linear separation theorem, not a consequence of mere absence of a PC refutation. Short-proof control. For any affine \(L\), the old system \(\{L,1-L\}\cup\mathrm{BOOL}\) derives one through degree one. It has a short complementary-parity refutation as well. Consequently, for every \(B\ge k\ge1\), all degree-at-most-\(k\) polynomials are in \(\mathcal C_B\), by multiplying the completed unit line. The generic consequence theorem is compatible with this whole family of easy parity contradictions: its conclusion is already satisfied, while the required separated space does not exist. This is a basic analytic control, not a comprehensive audit of known Res(\(\oplus\)) upper bounds. The latter remains worthwhile before advertising a general tradeoff.

passages.title: 1. The family with slack, the residual instance, and the canonical tree
passages.text: 1. The family with slack, the residual instance, and the canonical tree Labels are \(\{0,1\}^\ell\), \(n=2^\ell\); \(Q\) is a fixed subcube of size \(N=2^{\ell_2}\) (a set of \(\ell-\ell_2\) coordinates held at fixed values), \(O=\{0,1\}^\ell\setminus Q\), and rows are \([n+1]\). For \(e\ge0\) let \(\Phi_e\) be the set of pairs \(\rho=(R,\mu)\) with \(R\subseteq[n+1]\), \(|R|=N+1+e\), and \(\mu\) an injection of the other rows into \(O\); write \(E(\rho)=O\setminus\mu([n+1]\setminus R)\) for the \(e\) free outside labels. Then \[ |\Phi_e|=\binom{n+1}{N+1+e}\frac{(n-N)!}{e!},\qquad \frac{|\Phi_{e-1}|}{|\Phi_e|}=\frac{e\,(N+e+1)}{n-N-e+1}. \] \(\Phi_0\) is the compact subcube family of the weight step. A uniform element of \(\Phi_0\) is obtained from a uniform \(\rho\in\Phi_e\) followed by a uniform filling \(\rho''\), an injection of \(e\) rows of \(R\) onto \(E(\rho)\): every \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) arises from exactly \(\binom{n-N}{e}\) pairs \((\rho,\rho'')\), the choices of which \(e\) matched rows were filled last, and \(|\Phi_e|\,(N+1+e)!/(N+1)!=|\Phi_0|\binom{n-N}{e}\). The residual instance of \(\rho\) has pigeons \(R\) and holes \(Q\cup E(\rho)\). A bit term is a conjunction of literals \(b_{it}=c\); its rows are ordered, its pattern \(p_i\) on row \(i\) is the set of literals there, and \(C(p)\) is the set of the \(n2^{-|p|}\) labels consistent with \(p\). Under a partial assignment of rows to labels a term is falsified if an assigned row violates its pattern, satisfied if every row is assigned consistently, and otherwise alive with its uncovered rows. A disjunction \(F=(T_1,\dots,T_M)\) is ordered; it has at most \(r\) rows per term and at most \(w\) literals per row. The canonical tree \(\mathcal T(F,\rho)\) has as nodes the partial matchings \(\pi\) of the residual instance (rows of \(R\) to distinct holes of \(Q\cup E(\rho)\)). At \(\pi\) take the first term not falsified by \(\rho\cup\pi\): if there is none the node is a 0-leaf; if it is satisfied, a 1-leaf; otherwise its uncovered rows are queried in the term's order, each branching over the holes unused by the path, and a row with no unused hole is a dead leaf. A dead leaf has depth \(N+e\), and its leaf term vanishes modulo the row axiom and the column exclusions at degree two, so it does not disturb the leaf-partition identity of the image lemma . The height is the largest depth of a node, and \(\mathrm{Bad}_s\) is the event that the height is at least \(s\). Say \(\rho\) is \(s\)-rich if \(|E(\rho)\cap C(p)|\ge s\) for every pattern \(p\) occurring on a row of some term of \(F\).

An extension encoding in any family whose residual holes form a flat gains only from the residual pigeons and can record a residual row only by matching it to a consistent free label outside the flat, so it covers exactly rows with at most about log2(e/s) literals; a uniformly random flat defeats the pinned-row reader and keeps the lemma, leaving row widths between (1/3) log2 n and (c-1/3) log2 n open for M = n^c

passages.title: 5. The way around the refutation: a random flat
passages.text: 5. The way around the refutation: a random flat Section 3 uses that \(F_Q\) knows \(Q\). If instead \(Q\) is a uniformly random affine subspace of \(\mathbb F_2^\ell\) of dimension \(\ell_2\), followed by uniform \((R,\mu)\), then each label lies in \(Q\) with probability \(N/n\), a term of \(F_Q\) is alive only if its row is residual and its target lies in \(Q\), and the expected number of alive terms is at most \((N+1+e)N/n\). The weight step should accept a random flat: a basis of the direction of \(Q\) gives coordinates in which \(Q\) is \(\mathcal Q_N\), old affine forms restricted to \(Q\) are affine in them, the new bits are affine in the unary variables, and flipping a new coordinate is a translation inside \(Q\). This must be checked against the exact form of the kernel count and the coordinate-edge detector; it is not verified here. The theorem of Section 2 holds conditionally on \(Q\), hence in the random-flat family. For a heavy row \((i,p)\) with \(|p|>w\), the union bound gives \(\Pr[i\in R\text{ and }C(p)\cap(Q\cup E)\ne\emptyset]\le(N+1+e)(N+2e)2^{-|p|}/(n+1)\) for \(N\le n/2\), so rows with \(2^{|p|}\ge8Mr(N+1+e)(N+2e)/n\) are, with probability \(7/8\), all matched by \(\mu\) (satisfying or falsifying their term) or dead (residual with no consistent available hole, so their term vanishes modulo the residual axioms at degree \(rw+1\)). What remains open in the random-flat family is the middle range \(\log_2(e/s)\lesssim|p|\lesssim\log_2(Mr(N+e)^2/n)\), about \(\tfrac13\log_2n\) to \((c-\tfrac13)\log_2n\) for \(M=n^c\): such rows have typically no consistent free label, so the code cannot move them, and they are too many for the union bound. Deleting dead terms inside the canonical tree also needs the decoder to see the same dead rows, which the picked code labels can spoil. Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. On the literal frontier, the compact subcube family is now settled in both directions: readers whose rows carry at most \(\tfrac13\log_2n\) literals switch and compose with the weight step; readers with rows pinned into the fixed subcube do not switch, so the composition must randomize the flat and still handle the middle range of row widths. Parity terms remain the open core. Process assessment. The round-trip tool again fixed the code's shape before any proof text existed, but the fifth test case was launched without estimating its enumeration size (\(6188\cdot14!/2!\) restrictions) and had to be stopped after twenty minutes; the tester now prints the size and refuses cases above a limit, and the computation rules gain one sentence asking for that estimate.

Parameters: complete below \(n/\mathrm{polylog}\), a window above Take \(N\) polylogarithmic, as the high threshold needs, \(e=\lfloor(n/48r)^{1/3}\rfloor\ge N\), so that \(A\le\tfrac12\), and \(s=\lceil\log_2(8S)\rceil\) for a source with \(S\) readers of at most \(S\) terms each. passages.title: 1. The heavy-term bound on the compact family is sharper than stated
passages.text: 1. The heavy-term bound on the compact family is sharper than stated The proof of the heavy-term dichotomy bounds the probability that a row is residual under \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) by \((N+1+e)/n\), carried over from the slack family. passages.title: 2. The corrected obligation: distinct holes
passages.text: 2. The corrected obligation: distinct holes In a tree with hole queries, a window row \(i\) of an alive term, residual and with \(C(p_i)\cap Q\) a single point \(q\) (the typical case for \(|p_i|>\ell_2\)), is handled by querying \(q\): the branch \(X_{iq}\) satisfies the row, every other branch falsifies the term, and every other term wanting \(q\) is decided at the same node. A path therefore contains at most one query per hole, and a path with \(k_0\) heavy queries exhibits \(k_0\) alive window terms whose heavy rows are distinct and whose consistent holes are distinct . The obligation named last cycle is corrected accordingly: bound the probability that, under \(\rho'\), no term is satisfied and at least \(k_0\) distinct holes of \(Q\) are each the consistent hole of an alive window term. Paths with fewer heavy queries are paid by the encoding, with the answer to a hole query recorded in \(\delta\) (at most \(N+e+2\) values) and the row left unmoved. Why distinct holes are rare. For unary rows the consistent holes are the pinned labels themselves, and \(k_0\) distinct pinned labels \(x_1,\dots,x_{k_0}\) all lie in the random flat with probability \(\prod_{t}(N-2^{t})/(n-2^{t})\) over the affine rank \(d\) of the set, about \((N/n)^{d}\): a set of \(k_0\) affinely independent labels costs \((N/n)^{k_0}\), and even the cheapest configuration, a \(d\)-dimensional subflat of \(2^d=k_0\) labels, costs \((N/n)^{\log_2k_0}=n^{-\Theta(\log\log n)}\), superpolynomially small. For window rows of width \(w\) below \(\ell\), the analogous count is over the projections of \(Q\) onto the patterns' coordinates, with \(N2^{-w}\) in place of \(N/n\). A proof must combine this rank effect with the per-term rarity of the previous entry and with negative association of satisfaction events for terms on disjoint rows (the residual set and matching together form a uniform injection, whose indicator entries are negatively associated); shared rows and shared holes are handled by the tree rather than by probability.

passages.text: 2. A candidate counterexample and why it fails Fix a row \(j\) and, for every label \(x\), a distinct light pattern \(p_x\) on row \(j\); let \(F^{(j)}=\bigvee_x\bigvee_{i}[i\mapsto x]\wedge[j\text{ satisfies }p_x]\), a reader of \(n(n+1)\) mixed terms, one class per label. With probability \((N+1)/(n+1)\) row \(j\) is residual, every class is alive, no term is satisfied, and the classes whose label lies in \(Q\) are unmatched with all \(N+1\) residual rows alive at that label, so \(\nu(B_{\rm um})=N\); the \(n+1\) readers \(F^{(j)}\), of total size \(n^3\), always contain one in this situation. This looked like a refutation at size \(n^3\). It is not: every class whose label \(x\) lies outside \(Q\) is matched, because the occupant of \(x\) is pinned to \(x\), so after the tail query \(j\mapsto z\) every class with \(z\in C(p_x)\) and \(x\notin Q\) gives a 1-leaf under the preference. The adversary must answer with a \(z\) all of whose surviving classes have labels in \(Q\); if the patterns are designed so that the survivors of \(z\) are the \(k_0\) labels sharing a prefix with \(z\), this needs those labels inside \(Q\), which happens with probability about \((N/n)^{\log_2k_0+1}\) per prefix class by the rank lemma , so over the \(n/k_0\) prefix classes with probability at most \(n(N/n)^{\log_2k_0+1}\). Two lessons: alive pairs must always be weighed against the matched pairs of the same class, and the last probabilistic step is a rank bound for survivor sets , the labels of the classes kept alive by one light answer, all of which must fall inside the flat.

The sharpened obligation and a route that does not work By Section 1 with the recording rule, it remains to show: with probability at least \(1-n^{-c}/8\) per reader, no path has \(k\ge N/24-c\) heavy queries together with at most \(3k+3c\) light queries (paths with more light queries are paid by the encoding). On such a path the \(k\) triggers are alive pairs \((i_t,x_t)\), with distinct rows and distinct holes, of classes without a matched pair whose tails are satisfied by \(\rho'\cup\pi\), and every class with a matched pair is falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi\). The naive route enumerates the light answers: given \(\rho'\), a path's light answers are at most \(3k+3c\) holes among \(N+e\), a union of size \(n^{k+c+o(k)}\), against which the rank mechanism supplies only \(\Pr[k\text{ labels of one survivor set lie in }Q]\le(N^2/n)^{\log_2k+1}\), superpolynomially but not exponentially small in \(k\). The two do not combine for any \(k\ge2\); the reader \(F^{(j)}\) of the previous entry is harmless only because its paths have one light answer, so the union has \(n\) members. Hence the assembly cannot enumerate light answers; it must charge each light answer to the survivor set it keeps alive, and the quantity to bound is the affine rank in \(Q\) of the holes of surviving unmatched classes accumulated over at most \(3k+3c\) answers, with each answer's survivors weighed against the matched classes it also keeps alive. This is the open step; no part of it is proved here. Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. On the literal frontier the target is now correctly sized: trees of height \(N/8\) suffice, height \(6N+3c\) is already proved for every literal reader at every polynomial size by the trivial count, and the mixed-reader obligation is a constant-factor improvement of the heavy count, not an \(O(\log S)\) bound. Two decoder claims were corrected with fixes that do not change any parameter regime. Parity terms remain the open core. Process assessment. passages.title: 4. What the corollary does not give, and why the natural conditioning fails
passages.text: 4. What the corollary does not give, and why the natural conditioning fails The bad event needs \(k\ge N/24-c\) eligible classes with alive pairs at distinct holes and no satisfied class. In expectation eligible classes are \(\theta'\approx N^2\ln n/n\) times rarer than satisfied ones, so if the classes' events were independent the bound \(\min_\mu(e^{-\mu},(\theta'\mu)^k/k!)\le(e\theta')^{k}\) would follow. They are not: the reader \(F^{(j)}\) of the matched-first entry has all its satisfied and eligible events correlated through one tail row, and there the bad event is excluded by the survivor-rank mechanism, not by expectations. The natural repair, conditioning on the fates of all tail rows and applying the unary theorem to the pairs of the classes with satisfied tails, is not available: \(Q\) is the complement of \(\mu'\)'s image, so conditioning on \(\mu'\) at all tail rows of a reader, which may be every row, determines \(Q\) and destroys the rank lemma. Only a limited exposure can be used, and which rows to expose depends on the path. The correct organization, suggested by \(F^{(j)}\), is by rows: for every assigned row \(j\), all classes with a tail on \(j\) consistent with its label are unmatched, and a row whose consistent classes have labels of affine rank \(d\) outside \(Q\) forces \(d+1\) points into \(Q\). Turning this into a bound over all rows at once, with the bijection's dependence between rows, is the open step. Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. The mixed-reader obligation now has its class-level comparison lemmas, which are the correct replacement for the per-term rarity and hold for arbitrary pair sets; the remaining step is a correlation argument organized by rows, and the reason the obvious conditioning fails is recorded. Parity terms remain the open core. Process assessment. The cycle first tried an exposure argument and found that it pins the flat, which the earlier entries never stated as a constraint; it is now recorded so that later cycles do not retry it. No framework change is needed, and no computation was run.

passages.title: 1. The subclass
passages.text: 1. The subclass A class is a triple \(\tau=(j_\tau,p_\tau,x_\tau)\): a tail row, a light pattern (at most \(w\) literals) on it, and a label; its terms are \([i\mapsto x_\tau]\wedge[\text{row }j_\tau\text{ satisfies }p_\tau]\) for every row \(i\ne j_\tau\) (a full class). A reader \(F\) of this kind is a set of classes with pairwise distinct tail rows; labels may repeat. Let \(X=\{x_\tau\}\) be its label set. The tree is the canonical tree with the adaptive rule, the matched-first preference and the recording rule; \(\rho'\) is uniform in the random-flat family, \(2^w\le n^{1/3}\), and \(n\) is large. Two facts used below. Under \(\rho'\), a class with \(x_\tau\notin Q\) is matched unless the occupant of \(x_\tau\) is \(j_\tau\) itself, and a class with \(x_\tau\in Q\) is unmatched. A heavy query is triggered by an alive pair \((i,x_\tau)\) of an unmatched class, so its hole is \(x_\tau\in X\cap Q\); heavy queries have distinct holes, hence their number on any path is at most \(|X\cap Q|\).

passages.title: 1. Loading
passages.text: 1. Loading Classes are as in the previous entry (full, single-row light tails), but several classes may share a tail row; classes on a row have distinct patterns. For a row \(j\) let \(U_j=\bigcup_{\tau:j_\tau=j}C(p_\tau)\) and \(f_j=|U_j|/n\) (the loading of \(j\)); \(\Lambda(F)=\sum_jf_j\) is the loading of the reader, \(J_F\) the set of rows hosting a class, and \(L_j(z)=\{x_\tau:\ j_\tau=j,\ z\in C(p_\tau)\}\) the survivor set of a label \(z\) at row \(j\). Since \(|C(p)|\ge n2^{-w}\), \(f_j\ge2^{-w}\) for \(j\in J_F\), so \(|J_F|\le2^w\Lambda(F)\). Two facts. If row \(j\) is assigned a label \(z\) by \(\rho'\cup\pi\) on a path with no 1-leaf, then \(L_j(z)\setminus\{z\}\subseteq Q\): a class on \(j\) consistent with \(z\) whose label lies outside \(Q\) is matched (its occupant is not \(j\) when \(z\ne x_\tau\)) with a satisfied tail, so its term is satisfied if \(j\) is matched and its class is preferred and yields a 1-leaf if \(j\) is residual. The trigger holes of the path are contained in \(\bigcup_j(L_j(z_j)\cap Q)\) over assigned rows, and heavy queries have distinct holes.

passages.title: 4. The residual case
passages.text: 4. The residual case What remains for single-row full classes is a reader with \(\Lambda(F)>\lambda_0\) whose loading outside \(Q\) is below \((c+1)\ln n\). Its rows split into those whose union is covered, up to \((c+1)\ln n\) in total, by the consistent sets of classes with labels in \(Q\). If every row's dominant classes (those whose consistent sets cover half its union) have at most \(\rho\) distinct labels and the set \(X_{\rm dom}\) of all dominant labels has at most \(n^{2/3}\) elements, the rank lemma bounds \(|X_{\rm dom}\cap Q|\) by \(2^{c+2}\), each such label dominates at most \(\rho'\) rows by a degree hypothesis, and the remaining loading is outside the flat; the theorem of Section 2 then applies to the rest. The general case has no such degree hypothesis: one label may dominate every row, and a row's union may be covered by many classes with overlapping consistent sets (nested patterns give multiplicity \(\binom{\ell-w+t}{t}\) on a union only \(2^t\) times a single pattern), so the loading carried by labels in \(Q\) need not be small. This is the open step for single-row full classes; non-full classes and multi-row tails remain as before. Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. For mixed readers the window obligation is now settled for two overlapping subclasses, distinct tail rows and bounded loading, by two different mechanisms, and the residual single-row case is reduced to the interaction of loading with the flat's labels. Parity terms remain the open core. Process assessment. Identifying the loading as the parameter took most of the cycle, after a false start on unions over answer sequences that the sharpened obligation had already ruled out; the working context now names the parameter so the next cycle starts from it. No framework change is needed, and no computation was run.

passages.title: 2. Lemma: many rows with an out-class force a satisfied term
passages.text: 2. Lemma: many rows with an out-class force a satisfied term Given \(Q\), call a row an out-row if it hosts a class whose label is outside \(Q\), and let \(J_{\rm out}(Q)\) be their set. Each out-row \(j\) has \(|U^{\rm out}_j(Q)\setminus Q|\ge n2^{-w}-N-1\ge n2^{-w}/2\), so the out-loading lemma gives \(\Pr[\text{no term satisfied}\mid Q]\le\exp(-|J_{\rm out}(Q)|\,2^{-w}/3)\). Put \(r_w=3(c+1)2^{w}\ln n\): if \(|J_{\rm out}(Q)|\ge r_w\), a term is satisfied except with probability \(n^{-c-1}\).

passages.title: 3. The residual case
passages.text: 3. The residual case By Sections 1 and 2, a single-row full-class reader can be bad only if \(|X|>n^{2/3}\) and, for the given flat, its at least \(|X|-N\) out-labels have all their classes on fewer than \(r_w\le n^{1/3}\mathrm{polylog}(n)\) rows, while its in-labels, at most \(N\) of them, have classes on arbitrary rows. The trigger holes are in-labels \(x\) with a class whose tail row is assigned a label consistent with it: on a matched out-row the label \(\mu'(j)\) must avoid \(U^{\rm out}_j(Q)\); on a matched row without out-classes every consistent class gives a hole; on a residual row the answer must avoid \(U^{\rm out}_j(Q)\) and each such row gives fewer than \(2^{c+3}\) holes outside probability \(n^{-c-1}\) (survivor rank, as in the bounded-loading theorem ). Two estimates remain. (a) Rows without out-classes. Such a row has all its labels \(X_j\) in \(Q\). Rows with a single label \(x_j\) give holes in \(X_1\cap Q\), \(X_1=\{x_j\}\), which is small by rank when \(|X_1|\le n^{2/3}\) and otherwise puts at least \(|X_1|-N\ge r_w\) single-label rows in \(J_{\rm out}\), contradicting the residual case. Rows with at least two labels have \(\Pr[X_j\subseteq Q]\le(N/n)^2\), so the expected number of such rows that are matched into their union is at most \((N/n)^2\Lambda(F)\); a high-probability bound on the labels they contribute, a union of fixed sets \(X_j\) inside \(Q\), is the first missing estimate. (b) Gaps at out-rows. On a matched out-row, \(\mu'(j)\) avoids \(U^{\rm out}_j(Q)\) with probability at most \(1-|U^{\rm out}_j(Q)\setminus Q|/(n+1)\), and the holes it yields are the in-classes consistent with it; on a residual out-row the adversary chooses a gap in \(Q\). The number of residual out-rows is hypergeometric with mean below \(r_w(N+1)/n\), so at most \(2c+2\) of them outside probability \(n^{-c-1}\), giving fewer than \((2c+2)2^{c+3}\) holes. For the fewer than \(r_w\) matched out-rows, the holes are survivors of \(\mu'(j)\) inside \(Q\); each row contributes fewer than \(2^{c+3}\), and the number of matched out-rows whose label is consistent with an in-class is, by negative association, at most \(k'\) outside probability \((2u_{\rm in}/k')^{k'}\), where \(u_{\rm in}=\sum_{j\in J_{\rm out}}|U^{\rm in}_j(Q)|/n\) is the in-loading of the out-rows. Bounding \(u_{\rm in}\) with high probability over \(Q\) is the second missing estimate; it is at most \(\sum_{x\in Q}u(x)\) for the label loadings \(u(x)=\sum_j|U_{x,j}|/n\), and labels of loading at least \(3(c+1)\ln n\) outside \(Q\) are excluded by the out-loading lemma, so the estimate concerns how much loading the \(N\) labels of the flat can carry when every label outside it carries at most \(3(c+1)\ln n\). Both estimates are of one kind: a fixed family of sets (the \(X_j\), or the loaded labels) and the question of how much of it a random flat can contain; the rank lemma answers it for a single fixed set, and the sum over a family of size up to \(n^{c-1}\) is where the union bound fails. A moment bound over the flat, exploiting that \(Q\) has exactly \(N\) points as the sparse lemma did, is the natural next tool. Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. The single-row full-class case of the window obligation is reduced to readers with more than \(n^{2/3}\) labels whose out-classes sit on \(n^{1/3}\mathrm{polylog}(n)\) rows, with two named estimates of the same kind remaining; readers with at most \(n^{2/3}\) labels switch with \(2^{c+3}\) heavy queries at every polynomial size. Parity terms remain the open core. Process assessment. The observation of Section 1 is elementary and would have shortened the previous two cycles; the lesson, to bound the heavy queries by the labels available before analyzing rows, is recorded in the working context. Correction: self pairs Call \((j,z)\) a self pair if the only light survivor of \(z\) at row \(j\) is \(z\) itself: \(L_j(z)\cap X_L=\{z\}\), which happens when some class \((j,p,z)\) has \(z\in C(p)\). A self pair is light-loaded and light-good vacuously, but it has no light survivor other than \(z\), so the charge of step (E3), "every light-good pair has a light survivor in \(Q\)", fails for it; a reader with \(n\) labels on every row has up to \(n(n+1)\) self pairs, which would make (E3) vacuous. Self pairs never produce a satisfied term (the occupant of \(z\) is \(j\) itself) nor a hole (the hole \(z\) is the row's own answer), so they are irrelevant to the bad event and should be excluded from the loading. 1. Correction: self pairs

Call \((j,z)\) a self pair if the only light survivor of \(z\) at row \(j\) is \(z\) itself: \(L_j(z)\cap X_L=\{z\}\), which happens when some class \((j,p,z)\) has \(z\in C(p)\). A self pair is light-loaded and light-good vacuously, but it has no light survivor other than \(z\), so the charge of step (E3), "every light-good pair has a light survivor in \(Q\)", fails for it; a reader with \(n\) labels on every row has up to \(n(n+1)\) self pairs, which would make (E3) vacuous. Self pairs never produce a satisfied term (the occupant of \(z\) is \(j\) itself) nor a hole (the hole \(z\) is the row's own answer), so they are irrelevant to the bad event and should be excluded from the loading. Corrected definitions: a pair is light-loaded if \(L_j(z)\cap X_L\setminus\{z\} e\emptyset\); \(\Lambda_L\) is the number of light-loaded pairs divided by \(n\); \(u_{ m s}(x)=|\{(j,z) ext{ small}:\ x\in L_j(z),\ z e x\}|/n\); and \(V=\sum_{x\in X_L}u_{ m s}(x)\). With these, \(z otin Q\) lies in \(U^{{ m out},L}_j(Q)\) exactly when \((j,z)\) is light-loaded and not light-good, every light-good light-loaded pair has a light survivor other than \(z\) in \(Q\) and is small by (E2), so the count of such pairs is at most \(n\,u_{ m s}(Q)\), and \(V\le k''\Lambda_L\) because each small light-loaded pair has fewer than \(k''\) light survivors other than \(z\). Steps (E3), (E4) and (E5) then read exactly as written, since \(G_j\) already excluded \(z\) from the survivors. Step (E1) is unaffected: it uses \(|U_{x,j}\setminus(Q\cup\{x\})|\).

passages.title: 3. Clarification: which rows are assigned
passages.text: 3. Clarification: which rows are assigned The proof uses that every assigned row \(j\) of a bad path has \(L_j(z_j)\setminus\{z_j\}\subseteq Q\). A row is "assigned" if it is matched by \(\rho'\) or answered by the path before its last heavy query . This is the correct reading: if an answer satisfies the tail of a class with a matched pair, that term is satisfied by \(\rho'\cup\pi\) and stays non-falsified, so from then on the matched-first preference always selects a matched-pair term and no further heavy query occurs; a bad path's heavy queries therefore all precede any such answer, and the rows answered after the last heavy query are not used. Likewise a term satisfied by \(\rho'\) alone prevents every heavy query on every path.

passages.title: 4. General pair sets: the first obstacle
passages.text: 4. General pair sets: the first obstacle For a class with an arbitrary pair set \(P_\tau\), the events "alive and unmatched" and "matched" are no longer "\(x_\tau\in Q\)" and "\(x_\tau\notin Q\)", but events on \(\mu'\) with the ratio of the comparison lemma . Two of the six exclusions transfer directly: the survivor-rank step (E2) and the residual-row step (E6) concern only holes, which remain labels in \(Q\); and triggers at sparse holes, of degree below \(D^\ast\) over all pairs of the reader, form a matching of size below \(N/48\) by the sparse lemma whatever the classes. The obstacle is in the satisfaction steps (E1) and (E3): a dense label outside \(Q\) is occupied by a row pinned to it only with probability about \(1/(96eN)\), and which classes are matched depends on \(\mu'\) at the pair rows, so the out-loading of a row is no longer a fixed set and the negative-association product over tail rows does not apply as stated. The natural first target is the class of column classes , \(P_\tau=I_\tau\times\{x_\tau\}\), where a class is matched exactly when its label is outside \(Q\) and its occupant lies in \(I_\tau\); there the occupant of each label is a single uniform row, and the loading of a label can be averaged over occupants. This is the next cycle's task. Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. Parity terms remain the open core. Process assessment. The review was worth a cycle: the self-pair gap would have propagated into the pair-set generalization; the working context's switching paragraph is consolidated in a separate commit this cycle, since it had grown to over 700 words. No framework change is needed, and no computation was run.

passages.title: 3. The repaired target: bipartite full-column readers
passages.text: 3. The repaired target: bipartite full-column readers The natural role-separated version of full classes pins every row of a fixed set \(A\) of pinned rows, with all tails on the complementary set \(B\) of light rows, \(|A|\ge n/2\): class \(\tau=(j_\tau,p_\tau,x_\tau)\) has pairs \(A\times\{x_\tau\}\) and \(j_\tau\in B\). A class with \(x_\tau\notin Q\) is matched exactly when the occupant of \(x_\tau\) lies in \(A\), which has probability at least \(1/2-o(1)\) but is no longer certain. The proof of the single-row full-class theorem transfers with one change of exposure order: condition on \(Q\), then on \(\mu'\) restricted to \(A\) (a uniform injection into \(Q^c\)), which fixes the matched classes and the set of labels left for the light rows, and finally let the light rows map uniformly onto the remaining labels and residual slots. Given the first two, the survivor sets and the out-loading are fixed, negative association over light rows applies, and a consistent set meets the remaining labels in a hypergeometric number concentrated near \(|C(p)|/2\); the occupant events over distinct labels are negatively associated, so the out-loading over the exposure of \(A\) concentrates as well. Steps (E2), (E4), (E5), (E6) concern holes and light rows only and need no change. This is the next cycle's task, together with the round-trip tool for role-separated mixed readers, which needs no recording rule. Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. Parity terms remain the open core. Process assessment. The gap surfaced only when the decoder had to be written as code; the lesson, to implement a decoder before stacking results on its claimed correctness, argues for building the tool next cycle rather than proving further cases first. No framework change is needed, and no computation was run.

passages.title: 1. The compact tree and the pair space
passages.text: 1. The compact tree and the pair space Readers are role-separated as in the multi-row setting : at most \(M\le n^c\) terms \([i\to x]\wedge\bigwedge_{j\in J}[j\in p_j]\) with \(i\in A\), \(J\subseteq B\), \(A\cap B=\varnothing\), \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\), at most \(r\) rows per term, at most \(w\) literals per tail row, \(w\le\ell-\ell_2-1\), pin-free terms allowed; \(A\) is every row outside \(B\), so \(b=|A|\ge n/2+N+2\); \(A_y\) is the set of rows pinned to the label \(y\). The tree is the complete-term tree \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) on the residual instance of \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\), pigeons \(R'\) and holes \(Q\): the current term is chosen by the matched-first preference among the terms not falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi\), a term whose pin's hole is used or emptied while its row is unassigned counting as falsified; if its pin \((i,x)\) is alive, \(i\in R'\) unassigned and \(x\in Q\) unused and not emptied, the round queries the pigeon \(i\) over the unused holes of \(Q\) and, on every answer other than \(x\), the hole \(x\) over the unassigned rows of \(R'\) and the empty branch; then every uncovered tail row is queried in order. This is the tree of every recorded round bound after Lemma 2 of the complete-term rule ; a move is a light query, at a row of \(R'\cap B\), and the height of a path is its moves plus at most two per round. The pair space is that of the previous entry: an \(e\)-set \(S\subseteq A\), \(\Phi_e(S)=\{\rho\in\Phi_e:\ S\subseteq R(\rho)\}\), a pair \((\rho,\rho'')\) with \(\rho''\) a bijection of \(S\) onto \(E(\rho)\), and \(\rho'=\rho\cup\rho''\), a bijection from pairs onto \(\Phi_0^S=\{\rho'\in\Phi_0:\ S\cap R'=\varnothing\}\); given \(S\), \(R'\) is a uniform \((N+1)\)-subset of the rows outside \(S\), \(E(\rho)\) a uniform \(e\)-subset of \(O\), \(\mu\) a uniform bijection of the other rows onto \(O\setminus E(\rho)\), and \(\rho''\) a uniform bijection given the rest. Lemma A0 gives \(\Pr_{\Phi_0}[\mathcal E]\le\tfrac75\mathbb E_S\Pr_{\Phi_0^S}[\mathcal E]\) for every event when \(e(N+1)\le n/8\). Nothing else of the previous entry is used: the tree is the compact tree of \(\rho'\), and the slack restriction \(\rho\) appears only inside the code. This is the swap encoding on \(\Phi_0\) that the correction listed as a repair route and found blocked because "the displaced row's label must be visible to the decoder": the displaced row is the row filling the code label, \(\sigma\) makes its label visible as a value in \(E(\rho^\ast)\) or a slot, and the own-row rule removes the one pin the slot leaves undecided.

passages.text: 1. What the forty cycles produced, against the route The literal part was not an import of the classical lemma because the route constrains the restriction family: the residual holes must form a flat ( obstruction ), the restriction must preserve the compact base and the objects of the weight step ( preservation ), and the residual board has only polylogarithmically many holes, \(N\), with height budget \(N/8-r\) ( budget ). On such a family the uniform encoding argument gives switching for sources of size up to \(n^{4/3}/\mathrm{polylog}\,n\), the root dichotomy gives every source below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\), and above that a window of row widths remains in which the union bound over \(n^c\) terms is not available. From there the work proceeded by classes of readers: unary, single-row full-class, bipartite full-column, two-tier, activation-bounded, pattern-bounded, multi-row role-separated, few light rows, crowded rows, sparsely pinned two-role, the composition lemma on the pair space and then on the compact family, split rows, few tail rows, few wide rows, and pin-free single-row wide readers ( working context , the window theorem and its list). Each class needed a new tree rule, an encoding change, or a new probabilistic count, and several entries corrected earlier ones. This is a case list in the sense of the workspace rules. All of it is tagged here, in retrospect, to the first item of the remaining route, the general step, and it moved that item in no respect: the item's obstruction, recorded in cycles 171 to 174, concerns terms that are not literal.

passages.text: 1. Setting Labels are \(\mathbb F_2^\ell\), \(n=2^\ell\), rows \(0,\dots,n\). A form is \(L=\sum_j\langle a_j,x_j\rangle+c\), \(a_j\in\mathbb F_2^\ell\), \(x_j\) the label of row \(j\); it has degree one in the bits and, by the row axioms, in the cell variables, and the route here is binary. A restriction \(\rho'=(Q,R',\mu')\in\Phi_0\) has \(Q=q_0+{\rm span}(B)\) a flat of dimension \(\ell_2\), \(N=2^{\ell_2}\), \(B\in\mathbb F_2^{\ell\times\ell_2}\) of rank \(\ell_2\); \(R'\) a set of \(N+1\) rows; \(\mu'\) a bijection of the other rows onto the labels outside \(Q\). passages.title: 2. The general claim, and what the main goal needs from it
passages.text: 2. The general claim, and what the main goal needs from it The line's claim is Claim G (image or value): for a compiled source there are value axioms \(E\), linear equations in the bits or term values, such that the base with \(E\) stays hard and modulo \(E\) every block has an old image. The main goal needs the general step for the sources that short proofs produce, not for generic ones. Two facts from the record fix what that means at the first MOD level. A parity of the variables of the ordinary PHP becomes, in the bit encoding, a sum of arbitrary within-row functions \(a_0+\sum_if_i(b_i)\), a class of dimension \(1+m(n-1)\) against \(1+m\ell\) for affine bit forms ( recorded characterization ); so the simplest gate that an \(\mathrm{AC}^0[2]\)-Frege proof of the ordinary PHP uses is already a sum of low flat indicators, outside the class of the all-ranks one-level theorem . And a two-level source of this kind reduces without degree loss to the one-level unary affine family ( normalization ), for which the record has an inventory on which both recorded rank tests fail ( multiscale family , criterion gap ) and an exclusion at high rank only, with intermediate ranks open ( high-rank coverage ); the all-ranks theorems are for affine-bit families. The record's own caveat stands: the failure of the two tests is not an impossibility theorem, and no proof is known to use the inventory. The generic dense bit forms studied in the last eight entries are therefore a model of the frontier ( stated for bit forms ), not the simplest recorded unexcluded class; the simplest is one OR over parities of PHP variables at middle rank. For both, the value method asks the same thing of the base: hardness under linear constraints of rank far above \(n\), with right-hand sides of our choice. For bit-linear constraints that is Conjecture H1; for parities of unary variables the constraints are \(\sum_if_i(b_i)=e\) with arbitrary \(f_i\), a larger class. Recorded for it: the case split , which covers arbitrary old polynomial queries with right-hand sides of our choice at one degree per query, hence rank up to about \(n/2\), and the occupancy-probe theorem , an example where unary linear equations with the wrong right-hand sides drop the PHP to degree two.

passages.title: 4. Alternative (E): what the published methods need
passages.text: 4. Alternative (E): what the published methods need Read in the second paper (locators in the source audit ; statements imported as context). Theorem 5.5: a refutation of Razborov's \(\mathrm{PHP}^{m,r}_n\) over \(\mathbb F_p\), \(p>2\), with \(M\) extension variables \(z=Q\), each \(Q\) a polynomial of degree at most \(k\) in at most \(\kappa\) original variables, \(r>2pk\), has size \(\exp(\Omega(n^2/((M+mn)\kappa k)))\). The proof removes the pairs of terms of high quadratic degree in rounds. A round picks a variable by averaging; for an extension variable it applies an assignment of Hamming weight at most \(pk\) that sets \(Q\) to zero or to \((b-a)x+a\) (Lemma 5.3: set the variables of one minimal monomial to one and the other variables of \(Q\) to zero), removes every hole touched by \(\mathrm{vars}(Q)\), at most \(\kappa\) holes, and then splits the lines. The fractional pigeons are what makes the cleanup sound: an assignment of weight below \(r/2\) commits no pigeon to a hole. At the end the definitions are substituted, which multiplies the degree by \(k\), and Razborov's degree bound is applied to the surviving \(\mathrm{PHP}^{m,r}_{n'}\), \(n'\ge n/2\). Theorem 1.2 adds an XOR lift of the formula so that a random restriction brings extension axioms of polynomial size down to logarithmic degree. What this needs, against a compiled source of the ordinary PHP: (1) definitions in the original variables only, where the source is nested to the depth of the proof and the final substitution would cost \(k\) per level, the recorded multiplicative cost; (2) \((M+mn)\kappa k=o(n^2)\), where a source has \(n^c\) blocks for arbitrary \(c\) and dense blocks have \(\kappa\) of order \(mn\), so that the bound is void already for one dense block; (3) a formula that survives assignments of weight \(pk\) and the loss of \(\kappa\) holes per round; the ordinary PHP is falsified by two ones in a hole (the paper does not discuss it; this is my reading of why the fractional variant is used), and dense arity removes all holes in one round; (4) an XOR lift of the formula, which is not available when the formula is the fixed target; (5) \(p>2\); for \(p=2\) both papers point to the size-degree tradeoff, which needs degree above the square root of the number of variables and is void once the number of extension variables reaches about \(n^2\), the same limit as in (2). None of the five holds for the source of the general step, and (1) to (3) fail independently. The one idea with no counterpart in the notebook is the size measure itself (quadratic degree, removal of extension variables one at a time). It does not help here: every round spends holes in proportion to the arity, and the notebook's endpoint is a degree statement with the inventory entering only through a logarithm.

passages.title: 6. Estimates and selection
passages.text: 6. Estimates and selection Estimates, for the lines named only. That the value method (Claim G) advances the general step: about 5 percent, down from 10, because its hardness input turned out to have neither a proof method nor a test within reach (that its two mechanisms do not combine on the union source was known when the 10 percent was set). That an extension of the published extension-variable methods advances it: about 2 percent. The parked lines are unchanged ( Conjecture L is not sufficient; the level-one conjecture does not move the obligation). Selection. One bounded step, at most two research entries, on the weakest form of the wall: the parity-decision-tree depth (up to an additive \(\ell\) the depth of tree-like Res(\(\oplus\)) refutations, a standard fact that is not in the record) of the bit PHP on a generic subspace of codimension \(0.7v\). It is selected because it is sharp in both directions and cheap to state: a prover strategy of depth \(o(n)\) that exploits the linear relations of the subspace refutes the bit form of Conjecture H1 by Lemma T, and one of depth below the working degree of the recorded framework (\(B=k(D+1)\) with \(k\) of order \(\sqrt{n\log M}\)) ends the value method for dense forms, while a delayer strategy that survives \(cn\) queries would be the first technique on record that crosses rank \(n\); the motivation, a heuristic only, is that designs are often built from delayer strategies. First entry: try to build the prover strategy (queries that read one parity of many rows at once, using the relations of \(W\)); then the delayer, starting from the recorded closure technique and the observation that a pair is separated as soon as one form of its span is answered against its target. No computation is proposed: by the rule on nonvacuous tests, the conjectured depth \(cn\) exceeds the trivial bound \(\ell\) only on boards where the game tree over affine subspaces of \(\mathbb F_2^k\), \(k\ge n\), is out of reach. If neither strategy results, the value method is parked as a whole and the following review reconsiders the form of the general step rather than its mechanisms, starting from the simplest recorded unexcluded class of Section 2. Verification gate. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the compact family ( preservation lemma ), the observation of the previous entry used for Corollary U, Lemma R with its Hypotheses paragraph, the unary-query characterization, the label-parent normalization, the multiscale family, the middle-rank frontier, the statement of Claim G, and the literature section; from the paper, the passages listed in the source audit. Before drafting, the standing reviewer answered that the incompatibility statement follows in one line from the recorded observation with \(r=N+1\) (my own route, a union bound over the family, needed \(a>v/2\) and its claimed range \(\ell\ge4\) was wrong), that the record gives only \(\ell+d\) for parity trees, and pointed out the halving tree, which gives the corollary on the full base. On the full draft the reviewer confirmed Lemma T step by step, the halving count, the restriction of the tree to \(W\), Corollary U against the definition of the family, the counting sentence of Section 5, every statement of Section 4 against the paper text, and the presence of the five elements of a review; it found no error in the lemma or the corollaries and reported seven findings, all applied. (1) The inconsistency of the two axiom systems on the union source is already stated with Claim G; Corollary U is now presented as its quantitative form, and the reason given for lowering the estimate no longer counts it.
